description: We are a team of engineers specializing in mechatronics and computer science. We’re working on the “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions” challenge, combining software, AI, and data analysis with engineering to build a practical solution
summary: Asteron is an offline-first web app that monitors astronaut health on long space missions, built for the moment when Earth cannot answer in time. On the ISS a doctor is seconds away, but a message to Mars takes up to 22 minutes each way, and during solar conjunction the link is lost for about two weeks. Every day, Asteron reads each astronaut from a smart shirt, a one-minute check-in and a radiation dosimeter, covering physical and psychological health. An on-board engine compares each value with the astronaut’s own normal and with NASA-sourced limits, rates the case from normal to urgent, and shows on a 3D body where the problem is. Then it asks: can Earth answer in time? Using real NASA JPL Horizons distances, it calculates the earliest possible reply; if that is too late, the crew is told to act on board now. Every report is encrypted, signed and sent to the flight surgeon only when the link allows, so nothing is lost or exposed. Built on real NASA data and tested with 381 automated tests, Asteron keeps crews safe when help from Earth is too far away, and it can also help remote clinics and ships on Earth.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS
Asteron is an offline-first health monitoring web app for astronauts on long missions. It has two sides joined by a delay-tolerant link: a Station app for the crew and a Ground console for the flight surgeon.

  1. Reading: each astronaut is read every day from a smart shirt of the CSA Bio-Monitor class (heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, temperature, sleep, exercise), a one-minute check-in (mood, stress, workload, headache, rash, dizziness, vision change) and a radiation dosimeter.
  2. Engine on board: every value is compared with absolute limits, with the astronaut’s own normal over 14 days, with 3-day trends and with combined rules. The result is a level from 1 (self-check) to 4 (urgent), shown on a 3D body. Every rule cites its source.
  3. Link decision: using real NASA JPL Horizons distances, contact windows and solar conjunction, it calculates the earliest reply from Earth. If that is too late for the level, the crew is told: “On-board protocol now”.
  4. Secure store and forward: each report is encrypted (AES-256) and signed, then queued. It is sent urgent-first only when the link allows, and re-sent if lost.
  5. Ground console: the flight surgeon sees each astronaut with the age of the data, the alerts and the radiation dose, and sends advice back the same way.

Example: an astronaut on the way to Mars has a fever, a racing heart and low oxygen. Asteron marks the case urgent and the heart and lungs glow on the 3D body. The earliest answer from Earth is 4.8 hours away, so the crew acts on board now while the sealed report travels home.

BENEFITS

  • A clear instruction when Earth cannot help in time.
  • Each astronaut is compared with their own normal.
  • Physical and psychological health are tracked together.
  • Nothing is lost or exposed during blackouts.
  • The doctor never mistakes old data for new.

INTENDED IMPACT
Safer crews on the Moon and Mars, where help from Earth is minutes to weeks away (NASA HRP Risk 15). On Earth, the same approach can serve remote clinics, ships and isolated stations.

TOOLS
TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Zustand, Dexie (IndexedDB), Zod, three.js / React Three Fiber, Web Crypto API, Vitest, Playwright. Python for the NASA data scripts. Hosted on Vercel. No AI model inside the product.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE
Most health apps ask “is something wrong?”. Asteron also asks “can Earth answer in time?” and computes the answer from real NASA geometry. Judges can test it themselves in the Judge Lab: https://asteron-mission.vercel.app/lab

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

  • Real NASA data only: JPL Horizons, NASA-STD-3001, NASA NTRS and OSDR OSD-569, stored unchanged.
  • Honesty: crew data is simulated and labelled SIM, because real astronaut data is private.
  • Security of medical data.
  • Working offline.
  • Status is never shown by colour only.

EVIDENCE AND LIMITS

  • 381 of 381 automated tests pass.
  • Urgent cases caught 200 out of 200 times; false alerts 0.25%.
  • 52 out of 52 attacks refused.
  • 15 days of Mars blackout handled on board.
  • Limits: the rules are not yet reviewed by a clinician. Asteron is a self-support aid, not a medical diagnosis.
